name: Whisper: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
problem: Supervised ASR requires per-domain labelled audio, so one model cannot cover many domains and noisy conditions without retraining.
mechanism: Multitask encoder-decoder Transformer trained on 680k hours of weakly labelled internet audio with a multitask 'tokens, timestamp, language' objective: the decoder is conditioned on a detected source language, which forces it to also act as a language identifier and produces per-language training data for free. Trained with 30s windows of log-Mel spectrogram at 16 kHz, so inference always operates on a fixed 30s context regardless of the true utterance length.
notes: Venue confirmed against the PMLR v202 table of contents: 'Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202:28492-28518'. arXiv posted Dec 2022, venue 2023. This is the highest-adoption speech model in the repo: shipped as the OpenAI speech-to-text API, vendored by Apple (iOS/macOS dictation), Unity, and reachable from most cloud STT wrappers. INFERENCE-COST NOTE that matters more than the accuracy numbers: the fixed 30s context means short utterances pay for the whole window. Encoder prefill is over 3000 mel frames regardless of utterance length, so a 1-second utterance and a 30-second utterance cost nearly the same. Chunked long-form inference (30s slices) plus local agreement (Whisper-Streaming, 2307.14743) or chunk-aware batching is the standard mitigation. Decoder output token count, not audio length, is what varies. The paper reports no wall-clock latency or hardware throughput numbers, hence speedup_reported is null.
